chunk_map.heading: A skill's footprint is where its job lands
Composition is a live argument, so you read

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: a referent that never resolves for a reader holding the deck in order. Chunk0 line3 'You have a kit now: a test-strategy skill, a verifier, and a freshly drawn map of the moves worth packaging next' names all three parts in the same sentence, not a bare pronoun. Verified this is the arc-earned-vocabulary carve-out, not a forward reference: grepped the AE101 module registry (site/layouts/curriculum.js lines 51-56) -> M3=earn-the-trust (holds `author-test-strategy-skill` exercise, grepped), M5=learn-from-the-test (builds 'the verifier', grepped 8+ hits incl. line 63/71/82), M6=spot-gaps-build-the-loop (this file's own host module; its exercise draws the 'stack-map' -- What You'll Learn bullets 3-4, read directly). All three nouns are earned in modules that precede this lecture's own module-include position (spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md line47, after the M6 exercise + Human close, confirmed by direct read of that file). Chunk1 line9 defines **skill** in-chunk before chunk2 line17 reuses the plain noun 'skills' -- ordinary same-file reuse, not a violation. No pronoun/demonstrative in the body stays unresolved.

Harm prevented: a chunk locating another file by its position in a deck the reader can't see the shape of. Line26 '[Dino's skill stacking system](trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/skill-stacking.md)' and line28 '[Workflow composition lineages](...)' both name the document by title in the link text itself -- the exempted navigational-pointer shape, not narrative callback. Line3 'the passage you already sailed' doesn't locate a file by position either; it's a named-artifact recognition (rule1's arc-earned carve-out, verified above), and the maintainer block's own 'Figure' note (line45 raw / expanded) independently confirms the referent is `what-packaging-is.md`'s M5 passage chart. No 'the opening lecture said' shape anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: 'the X you did/saw' pointing at a beat the module's current set no longer carries. Line3's 'the passage you already sailed' + maintainer block's Figure note ('Base geometry is the M5 passage chart from what-packaging-is.md, byte-unchanged') both resolve to `curriculum/lectures/what-packaging-is.md`. Confirmed live and in-module: `learn-from-the-test.md` (M5, verified via the AE101 module registry) is the file that introduces the verifier/test-strategy/map vocabulary this lecture's lede assumes. The kit named in the lede (test-strategy skill / verifier / map) is backward-recognition of artefacts the student built across M3, M5 and M6's own exercise -- all three exist in the current module set; none is a dead beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal instruction anywhere in the body. The file is expository throughout (figure + two mechanics passages + a pointer to two reads) with no demo beat for a reveal to land after. Rule has no object here.

Harm prevented: a chunk whose only content is a wait-state, projecting as a slide that says nothing standalone. Chunk1 = figure + 3 defining bullets; chunk2 = 6 bullets building skill-to-workflow; chunk3 = thesis sentence + 2 named reading pointers + a closing instruction. Every chunk carries a self-carrying claim; none reduces to one context-dependent bullet.

Harm prevented: a header the chunk's own content contradicts. Header1 (line5) 'A skill's footprint is where its job lands' is restated almost verbatim by bullet2 (line10) 'Its **footprint** is wherever the job lands' -- true under the header. Header3 (line22) 'Composition is a live argument, so you read' is restated by its own next sentence (line24) 'How the field composes kits like this is a live argument with no settled answer' -- true. Header2 (line13) 'From skills to a workflow' is a transition/topic label rather than a full-sentence claim; read against its own chunk, bullets 1-3 cover per-skill wiring mechanisms and bullets 4-6 cover workflow-level checks and judgment -- the header's claim (skills compose into a workflow) does hold across the chunk's own content even unaided, and the maintainer block's Headers note (raw line53) already names this exact heading as adjudicated under `check_lectures §4`.

Harm prevented: a slide-visible tic. Ran `grep -niE '\bNot [A-Z][a-z]+\. Not [A-Z][a-z]+\.'` over the body view -> exit 1, 0 matches ('Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction absent). Ran `grep -niE 'one of the (most|best)|most useful|most powerful|most valuable'` -> exit 1, 0 matches (no self-grading superlative). No number-plus-retraction anywhere (body carries zero numerals as claims). No abstraction-noun stacks (concrete nouns throughout: skill, footprint, pier, leg, fix, orchestrator, routing, hand-off). Closest specimen to the anaphora/triad sub-item: line17 chunk2 bullet3's 'One skill names another as a precondition... One sequences and gates a chain... A rule in `./CLAUDE.md` matches a file or phrase... One hands its output to the next...' -- four short definitions share a 'One ___: label' cadence, but each leg names a genuinely distinct mechanism (explicit load / orchestrator / routing / hand-off) plus a fifth (leaf) breaking the anaphora outright -- this is a definitional enumeration, not a rhetorical repetition with an empty third leg, so it stays inside the rule.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: repo/maintainer vocabulary (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat-as-noun, mood, Connections) projected where the room can't parse it. Ran `grep -niE '\bsurface\b|\bfiring\b|\bcompendium\b|\bforcing function\b|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|\bConnections\b'` over the raw body (lines 1-31) -> exit 1, 0 matches. In-body terms (skill, footprint, orchestrator, routing, hand-off, leaf, pilot) are the lecture's own taught vocabulary, each bridged once per the maintainer block's Vocabulary bridge note -- taught concept vocabulary, not maintainer dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: whole-sentence bolding drowning the handle signal, or a bold count exceeding what the slide's own job requires. Existing maintainer accept-note (raw line36, 'Emphasis budget (Antti-directed "go very lightly on the bold")') documents and defends the exact spans present: chunk1 (slide1) carries **skill** + **footprint** as <=2-word sub-span handles on two separate defining bullets (bullet3 plain, matching the note); chunk2 (slide2) carries the four wiring-mechanism handles (**an explicit load** / **an orchestrator** / **routing** / **a hand-off**) plus **leaf** at its own definition -- five short handles on what is functionally a definitional/consolidation slide (naming five distinct mechanisms), matching the rule's own 'a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law' exception in spirit; *pilot* is deliberately left unbold per the same note. Chunk0 (lede) and chunk3 carry zero bold, also per the note ('Lede, SVG, and the two supplementary links carry no bold'). Read directly against the body and matches the note exactly -- pre-cleared per the dispatch-preamble instruction to check for an existing accept-note before flagging.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: a phase-less section present in long-read but dropped from the composed Slides deck. Confirmed its module include point directly: `spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md` line47 carries `[Composing the workflow](lectures/composing-the-workflow.md)`, the identical standalone-link include shape used by its three sibling lecture links immediately above and below it in the same file (lines 49, 51, 53) -- no structural difference that would make this file diverge from the mechanism the other three lectures in the same module rely on.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/lectures/composing-the-workflow.md` -> 'files: 1  slides: 3  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets ... oversized: 0 ... every slide is within limits.' Mechanical, exit clean, no accept-note needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: a lecture heading that reads as a task label rather than a claim, blurring the exercise/lecture mood split. Header1 (line5) and header3 (line22) are explicit declarative claims. Header2 (line13) 'From skills to a workflow' is the closest specimen to a violation -- it names a subject/transition rather than asserting a full claim -- but it fits the rule's own 'catalogue entries naming their subject' carve-out (parallel to the rule's own cleared examples 'Ralph', 'The numbers'), and the maintainer block's Headers note (raw line53) already reviewed this exact pair under `check_lectures §4` and cleared it as naming 'the composition concept the slide teaches in its variety.' Per the compendium's own principle (blocking = comprehension/trust failure), a label-shaped transition header that the chunk's content bears out is not a slide the reader can't follow -- non-blocking either way.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm prevented: a bullet that restates doctrine already done work (a), narrates the curriculum's own pedagogy design (b), or closes a slide with a koan restating its own header (c). Checked every bullet: chunk1 bullet3 (line11, post-diff) 'Nothing here is new except the placing. A move now stands at each point you used to steer by hand. Where no move stands, you sail that stretch yourself' adds two new pieces (autobiographical tie to the student's own prior practice + the uncovered-stretch boundary case), not a restatement of bullet2's footprint definition -- and the maintainer's own 'Lean pass (2026-08-25)' note on this exact bullet already cut the one redundant clause it used to carry ('Same passage, same drift, same fixes and guardrails' -- the figure shows it), i.e. this rule's own scrutiny was already applied here on the date the rule's calibration sweep is dated to. Chunk2 bullet1's closing clause 'Its footprint is set by the job, not by the phase line' is a distinct claim in its own right (backing block's `moves-are-not-phase-bound`), not a rerun of bullet2's chunk1 footprint definition -- it applies the law to a new axis (phases) for the first time. Chunk3's 'so there is no prompt to drill here' reads as register-shift orientation (this is read-mode, not drill-mode) rather than pedagogy-design commentary, and the maintainer block's Lecture-meta note explicitly names and keeps this exact clause for that reason. Closing line 'Pick the shape that resembles your day' advances new content (how to choose between the two reads) rather than restating header3's claim -- not a koan-kicker. No bullet in the file reduces to doctrine restatement, design self-reference, or a header-echoing aphorism.

notes: Rules 15 and 16 postdate the slides-judge template's blocking/non-blocking partition (which only lists rules 1-14 plus rule-7 sub-items) and are not named in it. Applying the compendium's own stated principle ('blocking = the slide cannot be understood or trusted as shown; non-blocking = polish on a slide that already works') classifies both as non-blocking here: a label-shaped transition header (15) and a low-value bullet (16) are density/effectiveness concerns, not comprehension failures. Both rows PASS on their merits regardless, so this classification did not change the verdict. Prior instance at this path (body_sha c3c2624f...) predates rule 16 entirely and predates shape_hash tracking (prefill reported 'prior instance predates shape_hash — cannot verify N/A validity'), so every row here is freshly judged against the current body, not carried forward.
